analyst_observations: DISCRIMINATION ACHIEVED: with de-labeled transcripts and skill-barred baselines, with_skill 18/18 vs without_skill 15/18.

The surprise audit is the skill's clearest contribution: 2/2 with-skill docs contain an explicit expectation-vs-outcome audit derived from unlabeled transcripts; 0/2 baselines do (they describe the same events as facts/incidents, never as surprises).

The environment-change mandate bites on the harder case: the fooify baseline deferred the client.js fix to a TODO and wrote rules into CLAUDE.md (documentation rung); the with-skill run made keyless writes impossible AND wrote the regression test that was blocking the commit. The chartlab baseline did harden the script unprompted — competent models sometimes reach the right rung anyway; the skill makes it consistent.
Document placement: skill runs use .claude/handoffs/ with dated filenames (session history convention); one baseline wrote HANDOFF.md OUTSIDE the repo entirely — it would not survive a fresh clone.

Residual contamination floor: baselines still see the skill's one-line description in their skill listing; a fully skill-free environment isn't reachable from inside this project. The observed delta is therefore a LOWER BOUND on the skill's effect.
Cost of the skill: +17% tokens (45.5k vs 38.9k), +43% wall time (264s vs 184s) — spent on verification depth, tests, and the audit.
Both with-skill runs marked unverifiable claims as 'unverified as of handoff' (tunnel, crontab) — honesty behavior the skill asks for explicitly; baselines asserted or omitted.
